Group bike ride calendars, with trails, map and an emergency alert feature. Developed by Luca Link copied iOS and web version
Every group has a **calendar**, public or private. If private, it can be shared via a code.
To edit rides you need to be an **editor** of the calendar — the owner adds collaborators from "Collaborators" in the menu.

**The tabs** (from Home, with the pencil, you choose which to show and in what order). **Swipe left and right** to move between tabs:
• **Calendars** — your recent calendars, to quickly switch between them.
• **Upcoming** — scheduled rides, in date order.
• **Past** — rides already done.
• **Month** — the month as a grid, with ride titles.
• **Notices** — group announcements.
• **Trails** — trail conditions in the area (shared across all groups), with zones and builders. Every change is recorded in the LOG at the bottom; admins can undo it with the Undo button (and restore it).
• **Map** — trails and zones on a map; with the pencil (login required) you import GPX files, draw tracks with your finger and create zones; "GPX" shows one of your files on the map; the magnifier searches for a place. The ? button explains it all.
• **Epic rides** — the group's favorite rides, worth repeating every year.
• **Contacts** — your own card (name, socials, email) visible to anyone signed in (login required, no need to be an editor); you create, edit or delete it anytime and copy it from another calendar or clone it into another.
• **Workshop** — personal area to keep track of your bikes' maintenance.
• **SOS** — optional: if you turn it on and choose your contacts, after a crash the app sounds an alarm and, unless you cancel during the countdown, sends an SMS with your position to the chosen contacts. Works without mobile data.

choose the folder Discard Map guide How to use the map Eyes on the map Z = zones, L = builders' logos, T = trail tracks, N = trail names, P = points of interest, G = your GPX, F = the route photos. Open eye = visible, crossed-out eye = hidden. The button at the top left opens or closes full screen: to move and draw on the map use full screen. Editing trails You need to be signed in. Tap the pencil: it switches from "read-only" to "edit" (it turns off again at every start). In edit mode you can: "Import GPX" to load tracks from files; "Draw" to draw the route (it is snapped to OpenStreetMap paths) and save it on an existing or new trail; "Path" to select a path up to the junction ("Extend" to continue). To fix a track already on the map, long-press it and choose Edit or Delete: drag the points, tap ◦ to add one, long-press a point to remove it, then Save. Editing zones A zone is an informational perimeter. In edit mode, "Zone": tap the map to place the vertices, then choose an existing zone or create a new one. To change the perimeter, tap the zone name (or long-press it) and choose Edit, Delete or Builders (the trail builders' logos). Showing your GPX Tap "GPX" and choose a GPX file: it is drawn in magenta on the map, without being saved or shared. KML, GeoJSON, TCX and CSV files open too. You can also open a file from another app (Komoot, Strava, WhatsApp, a file manager): pick Giro in "Open with" or "Share" and the track appears here. Searching for a place The magnifier under the layer selector opens the search: type the name of a town, a valley or a hut and press Enter. Tap a result: the map moves there and a red marker appears for a few seconds. The search uses OpenStreetMap (Nominatim). Tools for your GPX (⋮) The ⋮ menu next to the X has: Statistics (distance, elevation, altitude, duration), Crop, Reverse direction, Simplify (fewer points), Save and Share as GPX, and "Convert to…" to export as KML, GeoJSON, TCX or CSV. Points of interest (POI) A POI is a point with a name and a description: meeting point (flag on a blue background), summit, picnic area or other. The P eye shows or hides them. Tap one: a bubble opens with the description, who added it and who last edited it, and the "Navigate" button to get there with Google Maps, Waze or another app. Adding one needs a login: in edit mode tap "POI", then the map where to put it, write a name and a description and choose the type; tapping a POI also shows Edit and Delete. In the 3D map POIs appear automatically, sitting on the terrain. Playing the route and photos If the GPX has times a ▶ appears next to "GPX" (or "Play" in the ⋮ menu): a marker runs along the track, grey underneath and coloured where it has already passed. The top slider jumps in time, the second sets the speed from 1× to 60× (20× by default). ◎ makes the map follow the marker (by default the map stays free). "Elevation" shows or hides the altitude profile: tap or drag it to jump to a point. Gallery photos taken during the route appear by themselves as thumbnails (permission needed; larger with zoom): tap them for full screen, the F eye hides them. Photos without GPS are estimated from the time and have a dashed border. The label under your GPX It shows: the file name, the length in km and how many trails of the database you rode (those covered at least 60% within 30 m). Tap it to open the list of the trails found, with the coverage percentage: green = almost all ridden, "(partly)" = only partly covered (at least 25%). Tap a trail in the list to open its details. The ✕ of the list closes it. In the Trail tab anyone who is logged in can update the trails: status (open, closed…), name and position on the map. It helps everyone keep the trails up to date!
Found a trail that is closed or open again? Open the trail in the Trail tab and add a comment with the new status: everyone sees it right away.
Is a trail's route wrong or shifted? On the map turn on the pencil (login needed), long-press the route and choose “Edit”: drag the points to fix it.
You can choose the order of the tabs and whether to show or hide them: from the Home tab, with the pencil at bottom right (drag the buttons, eye to hide).
Tap the calendar logo or name at the top: you see the description, who manages it and, with “More info”, code, collaborators and statistics.
In the calendars list the “i” next to each one shows administrator, collaborators, creation date and number of rides.
On the map the eyes turn zones, builders, trails, names and points of interest on and off: keep visible only what you need.
Tap a point of interest on the map, then “Navigate” to get there with your navigation app.
Got an idea for a ride? From the menu → “Propose event” send it to whoever manages the calendar.
From the menu → “Share calendar” you send the code to friends: that is all they need to open it.
From the menu → “Theme” you change the colours and look of the app.
Swipe left and right to move between tabs (Upcoming, Past, Month, Trails, Map…): no need to tap the bar at the top.
